text: Five Navy bombers vanished in the Bermuda Triangle.
Then the plane sent to find them... vanished too.
It was December fifth, 1945. A routine training flight from Fort Lauderdale, Florida.
Five Avenger torpedo bombers. Fourteen men.
Their leader, Lieutenant Charles Taylor, was an experienced pilot.
But about ninety minutes in, something went wrong.
Taylor radioed that both of his compasses had stopped working.
He believed they were over the Florida Keys.
They were most likely far out over the ocean.
The weather turned. The sun went down. Their fuel ran low.
Their last messages faded into static.
That night, a rescue flying boat took off with thirteen men aboard.
It never came back either.
A passing tanker reported flames on the water.
No wreckage from Flight 19 was ever conclusively found.
Twenty-seven men were lost in a single night.
The Navy first blamed the flight leader... then changed its verdict to causes or reasons unknown.
Years later, this flight helped create the legend of the Bermuda Triangle.
Broken compasses. A storm. Or something else?
What do you think happened to Flight 19?
